description: Gigasim benchmark: throughput, the end-to-end latency of one block broken into the phases it blocks in, the queues that bound it, accumulated data size, and a section per store.

panels.title: Chain Height
panels.description: The newest block committed to every store.

panels.title: Blocks / sec
panels.description: Blocks that completed every stage: generation, block write, execution, receipts and the state commit.

panels.title: Write Throughput by Store
panels.description: Bytes each store was handed per second. This is the volume the benchmark asked the store to take, so it excludes whatever its engine amplifies that to; the per-store sections carry the amplified figure. state_store reads zero on a validator's stack, where SS is not opened.

panels.title: E2E Lifecycle — Time Spent
panels.description: Every stage a block passes through, on whichever goroutine performs it. Only blocking work is counted: waiting for another goroutine is excluded, and an asynchronous store contributes the wait to hand the block over rather than the write itself. The phases therefore sum to the latency of one block through the pipeline.

panels.title: E2E Lifecycle — Time per Block (amortized)
panels.description: The same breakdown divided by the block rate, so each slice is the seconds one block spends in that phase.

panels.title: E2E Lifecycle — Time Spent
panels.description: Every stage a block passes through, on whichever goroutine performs it. Only blocking work is counted: waiting for another goroutine is excluded, and an asynchronous store contributes the wait to hand the block over rather than the write itself. The phases therefore sum to the latency of one block through the pipeline.

panels.title: E2E Lifecycle — Time per Block (amortized)
panels.description: Stacked, the total height is the latency of one block through the whole pipeline.

panels.title: End-to-End Latency per Block
panels.description: Every phase summed and divided by the block rate: the critical path of one block.

panels.title: E2E Phase Latency (p99)
panels.description: The tail of each phase, which a mean hides. A phase whose p99 is far above its average is stalling on something intermittent rather than being slow throughout.

panels.title: Main-Thread Time Distribution
panels.description: Where the consuming goroutine's wall clock goes, including get_block, which is time it spent waiting for the generator rather than working.

panels.title: Executor Time Distribution
panels.description: Sampled from a fraction of transactions, set by TransactionMetricsSampleRate.

panels.title: BlockDB Queue Depth
panels.description: LittDB's write path for the block ledger. The control loop holds 64 messages and the flush loop 8; either sitting at its bound means block writes are blocking on it.

panels.title: Execution Queue Depth
panels.description: Blocks written to the ledger and waiting for the executor to pick them up. Full means execution and the state commit are the limit; empty means generation or the block ledger is. Bounded by StagedBlockQueueSize.

panels.title: ReceiptDB Queue Depth
panels.description: LittDB's write path for receipt bodies. Receipt writes block on the control loop when it fills.

panels.title: SC Commit Queue Depth
panels.description: The queues behind a state commit store write. The snapshot writer blocks the commit path when it fills, since a block is never dropped rather than snapshotted.

panels.title: SS Commit Queue Depth
panels.description: Blocks handed to the EVM state store and not yet applied. The commit path blocks on a full queue, which is what turns SS falling behind into slower blocks. Bounded by async-write-buffer, 100 by default.

panels.title: Block Hash Wait (p99)
panels.description: How long the commit path waited for hashing to catch up. Nonzero means the benchmark is running a full MaxHashLagBlocks ahead of the hasher.

panels.title: Account Population
panels.description: Hot accounts are the fixed set most transfers draw from, cold accounts are selectable but rarely chosen, and dormant accounts exist in state but are never read.

panels.title: Database Size on Disk
panels.description: Measured by walking each store's directory, on the BackgroundMetricsScrapeInterval cadence. The state WAL lives inside the state commit store's directory, so it is counted in both.

panels.title: Bytes per Account
panels.description: Total footprint divided by the account population, which is how the cost of state is usually quoted.

panels.title: Write Throughput
panels.description: What the benchmark handed the ledger, against what LittDB actually wrote.

panels.title: write_block Phase Latency (p99)
panels.description: The generator's blocking time appending a block and its QC, including the periodic flush.

panels.title: Write Throughput
panels.description: The changeset offered against what Pebble wrote beneath it. The gap between them is write amplification.

panels.title: commit_sc Phase Latency (p99)
panels.description: The commit path's blocking time in the state commit store, as the state DB measures it.

panels.title: Version & Snapshot Height
panels.description: The gap between the two is what a restart replays from the WAL. A snapshot height stuck at 0 means no checkpoint has been written and a restart replays everything.

panels.title: Internal Commit Phase Distribution
panels.description: The store's own view of its commit, one level below commit_sc.

panels.title: View Cache Hit Ratio
panels.description: The read path: reads served from the view cache rather than from Pebble.

panels.title: Pebble Disk Usage by Sub-Store
panels.description: The four Pebble databases the state commit store spreads its data across.

panels.title: Pebble Compaction Debt
panels.description: Bytes compaction still owes. Growing without bound means compaction cannot keep up with the write rate.

panels.title: enqueue_ss Phase Latency (p99)
panels.description: SS applies a block asynchronously, so what the commit path pays is the wait to hand it over. This rises only when the queue below is full.

panels.title: Apply Changeset Latency (p99)
panels.description: The enqueue is what the commit path pays; the sync apply runs on the draining goroutine behind it.

panels.title: Snapshot Height & Duration
panels.description: Empty until the checkpoint schedule has produced an SS snapshot.

panels.title: Write Throughput
panels.description: Receipt bodies go to LittDB and their tag index to the log-index Pebble database.

panels.title: write_receipts Phase Latency (p99)
panels.description: The commit path's blocking time writing a block's receipts. Bodies are flushed in the background, so this covers the litt handover and the synchronous log-index commit.

panels.title: write_state_wal Phase Latency (p99)
panels.description: The commit path's blocking time in the state WAL. It writes without fsync, so this is normally the smallest phase of a commit.

panels.title: Queue Depth
panels.description: The serializer and writer queues. Either at its bound holds up the commit path.

panels.title: WAL Size on Disk
panels.description: Bounded by the checkpoint cadence: the WAL is truncated below the newest snapshot, so a WAL that only grows means checkpoints are not being written.

panels.title: Replay Backlog
panels.description: How many blocks a restart would replay from the WAL right now.

title: GigaSim
